sections.content: A useful news response identifies the main point, selects the most important supporting detail and then gives a measured reaction. Use expressions such as en *resumen*, lo *más* *importante* es *que* and *destaca* que. A response should distinguish a summary of the report from your own opinion.

items.spanish: En resumen, la noticia trata de un fenómeno que todavía no tiene una explicación clara.
items.english: In summary, the news report is about a phenomenon that still has no clear explanation.

items.spanish: Lo más importante es que la fuente ha confirmado los datos principales.
items.english: The most important thing is that the source has confirmed the main facts.

items.spanish: El periodista destaca que todavía faltan pruebas independientes.
items.english: The journalist highlights that independent evidence is still lacking.

items.spanish: Mi reacción es de cautela porque todavía no sabemos si la información es fiable.
items.english: My reaction is one of caution because we still do not know whether the information is reliable.

sections.content: A good summary answers what happened and what matters most. A response then signals clearly where your own evaluation begins.
